{{Quote|You will receive the same treatment as the others.''"<br />"''What others?|Darth Vader and Starkiller, just prior to the latter's escape|<ref name="TFU2n" />}}
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], a '''battle''' was fought on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]. After the [[Battle on Death Star I|death]] of [[Galen Marek]], former [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], Vader sought to recreate his apprentice, collecting Marek's corpse and using genetic samples from the body to create a [[Aberrant clone|series]] of [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] intended as replacement apprentices. Most of the clones were [[Clone madness|deformed and insane]], though progress was gradually made, and a new generation of increasingly stable clones was created. Vader proceeded to [[Sith training|train]] the clones, though many of these subjects would eventually succumb to the madness that had claimed so many of their predecessors. After one would go insane, Vader simply moved on to train the next clone. One of the clones, called [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]], was only the latest in a long line of failures, though he was one of the most promising subjects.

During a training match with a number of [[Sith Training Droid]]s, Starkiller proved unable to strike down one of the [[Holodroid/Legends|droids]] when it assumed the shape of [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], Marek's former lover. The inability to overcome the genetic memories of Starkiller's template marked him as a failure, and Vader prepared to [[Death/Legends|execute]] the clone. However, Starkiller refused to submit and lashed out at Vader with [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], using the Dark [[Lord/Legends|Lord's]] momentary distraction to escape the training complex. Going through the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial forces]]&mdash;which included [[Riot stormtrooper/Legends|riot stormtroopers]], [[Jumptrooper/Legends|jumptroopers]], [[carbonite war droid]]s, and others&mdash;[[Garrison/Legends|garrisoned]] in [[Timira City]], where he was cloned, Starkiller fought his way to a landing pad. While on his way, he gained some help from [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] on whom he used [[Mind trick/Legends|mind tricks]]. Once on the landing pad, Starkiller escaped Vader and hijacked the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Lord's [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced/Legends|personal fighter]], escaping from the planet.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|I am strong, my Master, and I am getting stronger.''"<br />"''Show me.|Starkiller and Darth Vader|<ref name="TFU2n" />}}
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="TFUc">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (graphic novel)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' graphic novel]]</ref> the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] original [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Galen Marek]], had been dispatched to [[Corellian Treaty|create]] the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] as part of an elaborate scheme to distract [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] so that Vader and Marek could catch him off-guard and [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] him. While Marek was successful in his task, Vader betrayed him, revealing that the plan had been Palpatine's brainchild, intended to gather all of his enemies in a single place for quick elimination, and that Marek's own apprenticeship under Vader had been a sham. The Dark [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] had no intention of rebelling against his [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]], and Marek was left for [[Death/Legends|dead]], while the Rebel leaders were captured and taken to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] for personal execution by Palpatine. However, Marek refused to accept the state of affairs and traveled to the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], intent on [[Battle on Death Star I|rescuing]] the Rebels. Defeating Vader in a vicious [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]], Marek was given the choice of killing the Dark Lord and replacing him as Palpatine's apprentice, but he refused and attacked Palpatine. Marek died in the process, but not before the Rebel leaders escaped aboard his [[Rogue Shadow|ship]].<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

Seeking to recreate Marek in the year [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]],<ref name="TFU2c" /> Vader went to the [[Clone Labs|cloning laboratories]] on the [[Water/Legends|water]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] and saw to it that a [[Aberrant clone|series]] of [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] of his late apprentice was created. The process was very hit-and-miss, with numerous setbacks and failures caused by the inherent difficulties in cloning [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]]; many of the early subjects were deformed, and even the later, more stable clones still fell prey to [[Clone madness|insanity and psychosis]] within [[Standard month/Legends|months]]. As the subjects failed, Vader simply disposed of them and moved on to [[Sith training|training]] the next clone. Eventually, Vader began training another clone identified as "[[Subject 1138|Starkiller]]," Galen Marek's codename.<ref name="TFU2n" /><ref name="TFU2vg" />

==The escape==
===Starkiller's training session===
{{Quote|Those who came before you went mad within months, tortured by emotional imprints I was unable to erase. Some would not kill their father, others their younger self. With you, it is this woman. Now you will suffer the same fate they did.|Darth Vader, to Starkiller|<ref name="TFU2n" />}}
[[File:Starkiller_Kamino_Training.png|thumb|right|250px|Darth Vader provides Starkiller with a pair of lightsabers just prior to a training session.]]
When Vader arrived in [[Timira City]] on Kamino to check on the Starkiller clone, the subject had been in an isolation pit for approximately thirteen [[Standard day/Legends|days]], relying on [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to sustain his starved and dehydrated body. Vader was impressed with the clone's performance, releasing him from the pit and informing him that the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] mentor to Galen Marek, [[General/Legends|General]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], had been captured on the planet [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]]. Vader stated that when the clone's training was complete, he would be sent to execute the Jedi. Vader then inquired about Starkiller's continuing visions and memory flashes. While Starkiller elaborated on them, Vader decried them as the memories of a dead man, a mere side-effect of the cloning process that would eventually fade. However, Vader also made clear that if they did not fade, Starkiller would be of no further use to him. Vader activated a number of [[Sith Training Droid]]s and provided Starkiller with a pair of [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], initiating the training session.<ref name="TFU2n" />

Starkiller fought well in the training match, cutting down the [[Holodroid/Legends|holodroids]] with practiced ease, until only one remained. As he moved to cut down the remaining [[Droid/Legends|droid]], Starkiller halted when he realized it had taken the shape of [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], Galen Marek's former lover. Despite Vader's urgings, Starkiller was unable to overcome his instinctual love of her, and he could not attack the droid. Vader cut down the droid himself, before stating that Starkiller would receive the same treatment as the other failed clones. Before Vader could follow through on his threat, Starkiller experienced a sudden [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] of the original Starkiller's betrayal at Vader's hands. Starkiller decided to fight back before Vader executed him, turning on the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Lord and lashing out with a blast of [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]]. Vader was momentarily driven to his knees as his [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|cybernetics]] malfunctioned under the onslaught, and Starkiller used the opening to tear open the wall of the training room and leap out into the Kamino rainstorms.<ref name="TFU2n" />

===Escape into Timira City===
{{Quote|The Force gives me all I need.|Starkiller|<ref name="TFU2n" />}}
[[File:Starkiller_Escape_Kamino.png|thumb|left|250px|Starkiller leaps off the side of the Timira City spire.]]
Starkiller's training facility was situated at the peak of one of the spires of Timira [[City/Legends|City]], so Starkiller leaped into open [[Atmosphere/Legends|air]]. As he plummeted down the side of the tower, he used his powerful [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetic abilities]] to clear a path for himself, destroying exterior fixtures on the tower and blasting apart a [[Fighter wing/Legends|wing]] of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] that tried to intercept him. Crashing through a large [[Glass/Legends|glass]] dome at the base of the spire, Starkiller unleashed a powerful Force wave as he hit the ground, killing the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] in the room. He fought his way out onto the exterior ramparts of the city, making short work of any [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] in his path. The [[Riot stormtrooper/Legends|riot stormtroopers]] who joined the fray provided a small challenge for Starkiller, as their [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaffs]] blocked his lightsaber strikes, though they were no match for his [[Force power/Legends|Force abilities]].<ref name="TFU2vg" />

Fighting his way along the ramparts, Starkiller managed to re-enter the city, making his way to one of the smaller cloning facilities. Continuing through the [[Laboratory/Legends|labs]], he eventually reached an observation gallery overlooking the Timira City parade grounds. Starkiller suddenly had a brief vision showing him how to use a Force [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]], and he compelled the lone [[Unidentified stormtrooper (mind trick)|trooper]] patrolling the area to commit suicide by leaping through the gallery [[Window/Legends|window]] and falling to his death. The sudden activity caught the notice of the [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] manning the heavy [[Laser/Legends|laser]] emplacements above the parade ground, and they opened fire on the gallery, forcing Starkiller to retreat to the grounds. Battling through the parade grounds, he reached one of the main entrances, where he was confronted by a [[carbonite war droid]]. Starkiller used telekinesis to rip off the automaton's heavy [[Blast shield/Legends|shield]] before destroying the droid. Starkiller continued to use his lightsabers and the Force to [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat]] his enemies&mdash;including stormtroopers, [[Jumptrooper/Legends|Imperial jumptroopers]], riot stormtroopers, and others&mdash;he faced along the way. He also employed the mind trick power to get enemy forces to assist him by either fighting the other [[Troop/Legends|troops]] or by killing themselves. He caused severe structural damage along the way as well, such as at [[Barracks D4]].<ref name="TFU2vg" />

Starkiller happened upon one of the main landing platforms, where he fended off a horde of stormtroopers delivered by [[Imperial Dropship Transport/Legends|Imperial gunships]]. Making his way along a series of catwalks above the landing platform, Starkiller destroyed all of the troopers in his path before re-entering the facility once again. As he traveled down a windowed corridor along the edge of one of the domes, he was harassed by another [[Gunship/Legends|gunship]], which destroyed the corridor behind him as he fled. Exiting the dome, he saw [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced/Legends|Darth Vader's TIE Advanced x1]] docked on the adjacent landing platform. Destroying the communications tower in front of him, Starkiller used it as a bridge to reach the platform.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

Once on the platform, Starkiller drew heavily on the Force as he attacked the trio of [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transports]] guarding Vader's [[Starship/Legends|ship]], falling into [[Force Enrage|Force fury]]. He made short work of the [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] and cut loose against the stormtrooper reinforcements who arrived. The landing platform was quickly cleared, and Starkiller started toward Vader's [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]]. It was then that Vader himself arrived, telekinetically blasting open the double doors into the cloning facility as he marched out into the rain. Starkiller increased his pace and quickly boarded the fighter, taking off immediately.<ref name="TFU2vg" /> As Starkiller attempted to fly away, Vader grasped the ship with the Force, seeking to halt the clone's escape. After a brief contest between Vader's power and the ship's [[Engine/Legends|engines]], Starkiller managed to flee in the fighter. Following Starkiller's escape, Vader hired the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] to find and capture Juno Eclipse and bring her back to Kamino. Vader planned on using Eclipse as bait to draw Starkiller back to Kamino, where Vader would be waiting.<ref name="TFU2n" />

==Aftermath==
[[File:Starkiller_Cato_Neimoidia.png|thumb|right|250px|Starkiller on Cato Neimoidia]]
{{Quote|I knew it was only a matter of time before you returned. Now you will surrender to me, or you will die here where you were created.|Darth Vader, to Starkiller, just prior to their fight on Kamino|<ref name="TFU2vg" />}}
In response to the breakout, security at the facility was increased, affecting the development of [[Subject 1157]], another clone of Marek.<ref name="TFU2 website">{{LucasArts|url=games/theforceunleashed2|text=''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II''}}</ref> Following the information provided by Vader, Starkiller traveled to Cato Neimoidia, intent on rescuing Rahm Kota in order to discern the whereabouts of Juno Eclipse. Starkiller successfully completed his [[Rescue of Rahm Kota|mission]], although Kota did not know the location of Eclipse. Starkiller then traveled to the planet [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]], where he found [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]&ndash;in&ndash;[[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]. After having a vision about Eclipse and speaking with Yoda, Starkiller left for the [[Itani Nebula/Legends|Itani Nebula]] to find Eclipse. However, by the [[Time/Legends|time]] he arrived there, Eclipse had been [[Battle near the Itani Nebula|captured]] by Boba Fett and taken back to Kamino. Starkiller went back to Kamino to rescue her, and he there [[Assault on Kamino|fought]] against Vader, defeating the Dark Lord and finally reuniting with Eclipse. Vader was taken hostage by the Rebel Alliance, and they took him away to be put on trial.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|We have reports of the subject in the eastern trench.|An Imperial, regarding Starkiller, from the Nintendo DS version of ''The Force Unleashed II''|<ref name="TFU2vg" />}}
The escape from Kamino was first mentioned in the original version of the [http://www.lucasarts.com/games/theforceunleashed2 promotional website] for the [[2010]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''. The old version of the website featured the perspective of Subject 1157, another clone of Marek, from inside his [[cloning tank]]. Viewers could listen to audio logs about 1157's development, one of which mentioned the battle. The escape is also mentioned in the current version of the website, which changed in format after the game was released. The battle had its first appearance in author [[Sean Williams]]' 2010 [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|novelization]] of ''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II''. The escape from Kamino was the first level in the video game.

The Flash-based game [[Escape from Kamino (game)|''Escape from Kamino'']] also recreated the level. The game was found on the official [[Wikipedia:Facebook|Facebook]] page for ''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II''.<ref name="FB: Escape">{{Facebook|username=StarWarsTheForceUnleashedII|url=StarWarsTheForceUnleashedII/posts/165979323420846|name=''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II''|date=October27, 2010|quote=Facebook fans - Escape From Kamino, a flash de-make of Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II, is now live! Click the tab at the top of the page!|nobackup=1}}</ref>

While the [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]], [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]], and [[Wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]]/[[Wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PlayStation 3]] versions of the game differ from each other, the storyline remains basically the same. This article follows the Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 version, since it remains closer to the novel, which is considered the higher level of [[canon]]icity.<ref name="canon">{{SWArchive|url=vault/books/tfu2_books/index.html?page=1|text=This Week: Experience ''The Force Unleashed II'' Story in Books}}</ref> The story presented in the novel cuts down the battle considerably; Starkiller jumps out of the training facility directly to the landing platform that holds Vader's starfighter. He uses the Force to knock down the three AT-STs before boarding the fighter. Also, Vader uses the Force to grip the fighter, although Starkiller manages to break free.

The mission in the Wii version follows a different path through the facility, although the introduction is the same. Starkiller lands outside after escaping Vader by sliding down the side of the facility before fighting through Imperial troops. In one part of the facility, he uses Force lightning on a fan to stop its blades and safely pass through. In another part, he fights Vader, who Force chokes him. An explosion then knocks Starkiller down a [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolift]] shaft and outside the facility. After fighting through more troops, he finds himself in the training grounds, which are protected by pop-up [[Autoturret/Legends|turrets]]. Re-entering the facility, Starkiller fights more troops and faces Vader again. They fight, and Starkiller shoves him away to escape on a turbolift, which takes him to a corridor filled with troops. Past the corridor are two AT-STs, one of which he stabs with his lightsaber and the other he knocks aside after Force-gripping a tower. He then throws the tower at Vader, allowing him to escape aboard the TIE fighter.

The level for the Nintendo DS version is played in [[Wikipedia:2D computer graphics|2D mode]], rather than in the [[Wikipedia:3D computer graphics|3D mode]] of the other versions of the game. As with the Wii version, the overall story remains largely the same, in that Starkiller fights his way through Imperial troops on Kamino. At certain parts, he must be careful not to touch a green-colored substance that could harm him. Starkiller also uses his lightsabers to destroy several fans along his way so that he may go through those sections of the level. After fighting through Imperial forces inside and outside buildings, Starkiller comes to a landing pad where Vader's TIE fighter is sitting. Although Vader comes out to confront Starkiller, the latter manages to escape in the starfighter.
